name: vector-proof-free
title: Vector proof (free figure)
tagline: Author any vector figure point-by-point — each point a position vector in {a, b}, joined by chosen edges; base arrows, amber segment highlighter, derived routes / k / collinearity.
description: The GCSE grade-9 vector-geometry proof figure, drawn freely rather than from a preset shape. The author names every point as a position vector in a chosen basis {a, b} — directly (at: [2, 4] = 2a + 4b, supports decimals and exact [num,den] fractions) or by construction (a midpoint, a ratio point on a segment, a point on an extended line) — then lists the edges to draw. The base-vector arrows appear automatically on any edge whose vector is exactly ±a or ±b (override with arrows), with their labels (a, 2a, −b, …) derived. A required per-segment amber highlighter (highlight: [["E","D"],["O","C"]]) draws a highlighter behind chosen lines — for "show these two are parallel". The same exact rational engine as the preset then expresses any route between two named points (express: ["OH","CI"]) or a single find ("OP") in terms of a and b in simplest form, finds the scalar k when as:"scalar", and proves three points collinear (one route a scalar multiple of another sharing a point). Everything is laid out from the two basis directions so the not-to-scale figure stays internally consistent (midpoints look like midpoints, collinear points line up) and the figure cannot lie — there is nowhere to author a route value. This draws the figures the preset cannot: a trapezium, a tiling of parallelograms, two concentric hexagons with both rings labelled (inner a,b / outer 2a,2b), a straight-line + triangle configuration. The target answer occludes for a question; the worked route reveals one line at a time for a staged build.
whenToUse: Reach for this for vector-proof figures the preset cannot draw — a trapezium, tiled parallelograms, two labelled concentric hexagons, a straight-line + triangle — anything authored point by point. For the standard triangle OAB / parallelogram / regular hexagon (vertex algebra built in) prefer geometry/vector-proof-preset; for column vectors on a squared grid use geometry/vectors. Author: basis ({ a: <deg>, b: <deg> } — the two base-vector directions on screen, math y-up; e.g. {a:90,b:0} for an upright a and a rightward b, {a:120,b:60} for a hexagon, default {a:115,b:35}); labels ({ a, b } — the base-vector letters, default a, b — relabel to p, q, x, y …); points (each name + one of at / midpoint / divide / extend — at is the position vector [p,q] in {a,b}; constructions reference earlier points); edges (the segments to draw as [U,W] pairs — drawing is explicit, since one point cloud supports many figures); arrows (optional — [{ edge:[U,W], label? }] to force/label a base arrow; omit and any ±a/±b edge is auto-arrowed); highlight ([[U,W],…] amber highlighter behind those segments — for "show ED and OC are parallel"). Then a task: { find:"OP" } expresses that route in terms of a and b; { find:"OP", as:"scalar" } writes OP = k(…) and gives k; { express:["OH","CI","FK"] } expresses several routes (one answer line each — the "write each vector in terms of a and b" build); { prove:["A","M","X"] } proves those three lie on a straight line. occlude the answer for a question; solution.show renders the worked/listed routes below the figure, solution.reveal limits it to the first N lines for a staged build (base = figure + question, then one line per stage). Keep the same basis and labels across a lesson so pupils track one diagram. Synonyms a teacher might use: vector proof, vectors in terms of a and b, express the vector, position vector, ratio point, midpoint, point on the line extended, prove collinear, show points lie on a straight line, show vectors are parallel, scalar multiple, find the value of k, trapezium vectors, hexagon vectors, grade 9 vectors.
tags: in terms of a and b

basis.description: The two base-vector DIRECTIONS on screen, in degrees, measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis (math y-up: 0 = right, 90 = up). a points along basis.a, b along basis.b. These only set the drawing frame (the not-to-scale tilt); they never change any derived vector. Default { a: 115, b: 35 } — a clean oblique pair. For an upright/right figure use { a: 90, b: 0 }; for a regular hexagon use { a: 120, b: 60 }.

a.description: Direction of base vector a, degrees anticlockwise from +x (math y-up). Default 115.

b.description: Direction of base vector b, degrees anticlockwise from +x (math y-up). Default 35.

labels.description: The letters the two base vectors are drawn and written with. Default a and b. Relabel to p, q / x, y etc. — threaded through every arrow label, route line and answer.

a.description: Letter for base vector a, e.g. "p". Default "a".

b.description: Letter for base vector b, e.g. "q". Default "b".

name.description: The point's single-letter name — ANY uppercase letter (A, O, P, X, …). Names are free; there are no reserved base vertices. Must be unique within points.

oneOf.description: An integer or decimal coefficient, e.g. 2, -1, 0.5.
An exact fraction as [numerator, denominator], e.g. [1, 3] for ⅓, [-2, 3] for −⅔.

items.description: One coefficient of a base vector: an integer, a decimal, or an exact [num, den] fraction pair.

at.description: The point's position vector as [p, q] = p·a + q·b in the basis {a, b}. e.g. [0, 0] is the common origin O, [1, 0] is a, [0, 1] is b, [1, 1] is a + b, [2, 4] is 2a + 4b, [1, 0.5] or [[1,1],[1,2]] is a + ½b. Use this OR exactly one construction (midpoint / divide / extend).

midpoint.description: This point is the MIDPOINT of the segment between two EARLIER points, e.g. ["B","C"] for "M is the midpoint of BC".

of.description: An ordered pair of existing point names [start, end].

ratio.description: Two positive whole numbers [first, second] — the two parts of the ratio, in the order the construction names them.

divide.description: This point divides a segment INTERNALLY. of ["A","B"], ratio [1,3] means "P on AB with AP:PB = 1:3" — the ratio is (start→point):(point→end). Both named points must be earlier in the list.

of.description: An ordered pair of existing point names [start, end].

ratio.description: Two positive whole numbers [first, second] — the two parts of the ratio, in the order the construction names them.

extend.description: This point lies on a segment EXTENDED beyond its end. of ["A","B"], ratio [3,2] means "X on AB extended with AB:BX = 3:2" — the ratio is (whole segment start→end):(end→point). A dashed extension is drawn from the end vertex out to the point.

dot.description: Draw a filled dot at this point (in addition to its label). Default: dots are drawn on constructed (midpoint/divide/extend) points and OMITTED on direct `at` polygon vertices, which read as corners. Set true to force a dot, false to suppress one.

highlight.description: Draw this point's dot + label in amber (result/emphasis). Default false.

points.description: Every point in the figure. Each names exactly one of at (a position vector [p,q] in {a,b}) OR a construction (midpoint / divide / extend) referencing EARLIER points in this list (they resolve top to bottom). Give the common origin as a point at [0,0] (any letter, conventionally O). All points are labelled; dots appear on constructed points by default (override with dot).

items.description: A segment to DRAW between two named points, e.g. ["O","A"]. Order does not matter for drawing.

edges.description: The segments to DRAW, each a pair of point names [U,W]. The drawing is explicit because one set of points supports many figures (a trapezium vs a triangle on the same corners). A figure with no edges shows just the labelled points.

edge.description: The edge [U,W] to put a base-vector arrowhead + label on.

label.description: Override the auto-derived label (e.g. force "2a"). Omit to derive it from the edge's vector.

arrows.description: Which edges carry a base-vector arrowhead and label. OMIT this and the SPOKES from the common origin O (the point at [0,0]) whose vector is a pure ±k·a or ±k·b are auto-arrowed and labelled (OA = a, OB = b, OA = 2a — the usual case). Other edges that happen to run parallel to a base vector (a hexagon side, a tile edge) are figure content and are NOT auto-arrowed — declare any of those here, e.g. [{ edge:["A","B"] }, { edge:["O","C"], label:"8b" }]. Each entry: edge [U,W] (oriented for the label) + optional label override. Give an empty array to suppress all auto-arrows. If an arrowed edge is not in `edges`, the spoke line is drawn under the arrow so no arrowhead floats.

items.description: A segment to DRAW between two named points, e.g. ["O","A"]. Order does not matter for drawing.

highlight.description: Segments to draw an amber HIGHLIGHTER behind (a thick translucent stroke under the line) — the "highlight these line sections" feature, e.g. [["E","D"],["O","C"]] for "show ED and OC are parallel". Result/emphasis semantics; pairs with a prove/express task.

task.description: What the figure asks. Omit for a plain labelled diagram.

find.description: A target route as two point names, e.g. "OP", "MN" (from the first letter's point to the second's). Expresses this vector in terms of a and b (or finds k with as:"scalar").

express.description: A LIST of routes to express, e.g. ["OH","CI","FK"]. Each becomes one answer line ("OH = 2b", "CI = −a + b"). Pair with solution.show and stage with solution.reveal to reveal one per click — the "write each vector in terms of a and b" build. Use instead of find when the figure asks for several vectors.

as.description: "vector" (default): express find as pa + qb. "scalar": write find as k(…) over a coprime integer bracket and give k — the "find the value of k" question.

scalarName.description: The letter for the scalar in as:"scalar". Default "k".

prove.description: Three point names to prove collinear, e.g. ["A","M","X"]. The engine takes the first as the shared point, derives the two routes from it, and shows one is a scalar multiple of the other → the three lie on a straight line.

occlude.description: Hide the final answer (k, the vector, or each expressed route) as "?" — the question hook. The figure and any shown working up to the answer stay visible. Default false.

solution.description: The worked route shown below the figure (also the answer list for task.express). Omit (or show:false) for a question / answer space.

show.description: Render the worked route lines (the derivation in terms of a and b), or — with task.express — the list of routes. Default false: figure + question only.

reveal.description: Show only the first N lines — for a STAGED build (one line per stage). Default: all lines. N = 0 shows the figure and question with no working (a sensible base stage).

highlightAnswer.description: Amber the final answer line. Default false.

arrows.description: Draw the base-vector arrows + labels. Default true.

dots.description: Draw point dots (where a point's own dot default/flag asks for one). Default true; false suppresses all dots.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
